images.title: The minute hand from 2 to 7
images.purpose: Show the minute hand starting at 2 and moving 25 minutes to 7, the five 1/12 steps it makes and the 5/12 turn.
images.composition: A large clock face on the left with the swept part shaded and the working written on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. CLOCK, centre (480, 408): a circle 560 px across (thin dark #2B2B2B outline, 6 px) with a pale cream #FFF8E7 fill, the numbers 1 to 12 in dark bold sans-serif (40 px) placed round inside the rim at their usual places (12 at the top), 60 tiny minute marks (thin grey #6B7280 ticks, 12 px long) round the rim, and 12 longer ticks (24 px) at the numbers. A hub dot 24 px across at the centre. The starting hand is a teal #0072B2 line (10 px) from the centre to just inside the number 2, labelled starts at 2 (34 px, bold, dark) outside the rim at (790, 190). The stopping hand is an amber #E69F00 line (10 px) from the centre to just inside the number 7, labelled stops at 7 (34 px, bold, dark) outside the rim at (420, 760). The part of the clock swept from the starting hand to the stopping hand, going the way a clock moves, is filled pale amber (35 percent opaque) and cut by 4 thin dark lines from the centre at 3, 4, 5 and 6 so that, with the two hands, there are exactly 5 equal steps, each step labelled with a small dark 1/12 (28 px) inside at mid radius. A curved arrow (amber, arrowhead) on a circle of radius 330 px runs the way a clock moves from 2 to 7. RIGHT SIDE: five lines of dark bold text (46 px) left aligned at x 900: 25 minutes at y 230, 25 ÷ 5 = 5 steps at y 310, 5 steps of 1/12 at y 390, = 5/12 turn at y 470, and, smaller (38 px) at y 560, 5 minutes is a 1/12 turn. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
the numbers 1 to 12 in the wrong places
more or fewer than 5 equal steps between the two hands
images.takeaway: 25 minutes is 5 steps of 5 minutes, so the minute hand makes a 5/12 turn and stops at 7.
images.description: A clock with the minute hand starting at 2 and stopping at 7, the five 1/12 steps between shaded, and 25 minutes = 5/12 turn written beside it.
images.context: Concept image for Minutes and Turns of the Minute Hand. It follows the idea of the clock faces with the minute hand's starting place in your maths book and shows the concept's own example of a hand that starts at 2 and moves 25 minutes.
images.teaching_notes: Count the steps from 2 to 7 with a finger. The slip to watch is starting the count from 12 instead of from where the hand starts.

image_decisions.why: The clock with the shaded steps from 2 to 7 shows the minutes, the turn and the stopping place together.
